title: Why Is Trump Strangling Cuba?
author: Juan David Rojas
content:

Amid a US-imposed oil blockade, Cuba is facing a worsening [humanitarian
catastrophe](https://www.ohchr.org/en/press-releases/2026/02/un-experts-
condemn-us-executive-order-imposing-fuel-blockade-cuba), including daily
electricity blackouts and shortages of food, medicine, and other basic goods.
The lack of fuel has put pressure on the country's water systems and forced
commercial airlines to cancel flights. The oil blockade comes after more than
60 years of sanctions, including an embargo on trade between the US and the
island nation, as well as secondary [sanctions
](https://www.miamiherald.com/news/nation-
world/world/americas/cuba/article306224076.html)on foreign firms that do
business with the regime.

In the wake of the Trump administration's Jan. 3
[kidnapping](https://www.cnn.com/world/live-news/venezuela-explosions-caracas-
intl-hnk-01-03-26) of Venezuelan dictator Nicolas Maduro, Caracas, under
pressure from the US,
[ceased](https://www.ft.com/content/f844ce4a-82b3-4ca0-969c-679f9ce3018b) all
oil shipments to Cuba-a vital source of fuel for millions of Cubans. Mexico
has [likewise ended](https://www.reuters.com/business/energy/mexican-oil-
shipments-cuba-currently-halted-president-
says-2026-02-09/#:~:text=By%20Reuters,Isabel%20Martinez%20and%20Sarah%20Morland)
oil exports to Cuba amid tariff threats from the White House. More often than
not, residents of the capital, Havana, [lack
power](https://www.cbc.ca/news/world/cuba-fuel-crisis-9.7083047) amid ongoing
rationing of electricity. Food and health [shortages
](https://www.paho.org/en/crisis-situation-cuba)are also increasingly acute in
the culmination of an unprecedented humanitarian crisis
[engineered](https://www.wola.org/analysis/understanding-failure-of-us-cuba-
embargo/) largely by Washington. Sadly, all of this suffering is likely aimed
at [appeasing neoconservatives](https://unherd.com/2025/10/how-miami-hawks-
hijacked-trumps-foreign-policy/) in Miami.

In the final days of his first presidency in 2021, Trump
[designated](https://cu.usembassy.gov/u-s-announces-designation-of-cuba-as-a-
state-sponsor-of-terrorism/) Cuba as a State Sponsor of Terrorism (SSOT) - a
move publicly pushed for by now Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who was a
senator at the time. The designation, coupled with decades of mismanagement
from the Cuban Communist Party, effectively
[destroyed](https://americanaffairsjournal.org/2025/08/the-cuban-conundrum-
fear-loathing-and-stagnation-in-havana-and-miami/#notes) the island's tourism-
dependent economy. After 2021, dozens of foreign firms [pulled out
](https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/cuba-seeks-foreign-investment-
thumbing-nose-us-sanctions-2023-11-06/)of Cuba on pain of doing business with
a "state sponsor of terrorism"; the Biden administration also announced that
foreigners who visited the island would be [barred](https://www.the-
independent.com/travel/news-and-advice/cuba-tourism-visa-us-
trump-b2173792.html) from visa‑free travel to the US. In contrast to record
arrivals elsewhere in the Caribbean, Cuba received just [1.8
million](https://www.upi.com/Top_News/World-News/2026/02/03/latam-cuba-
tourism-decline/5611770143806/) visitors in 2025 compared to over 4 million in
2019.

The post-pandemic crisis has been compared to the "Special Period," following
the collapse of the Soviet Union, which had subsidized its socialist ally
until 1991. Beginning in the early 2000s, Cuba deepened ties with Hugo
Chavez's Venezuela, which began sending billions in crude petroleum for the
island's oil-fired plants as well as resale on the global market. As Venezuela
has struggled with its own**** crises since the 2010s, oil shipments to Havana
declined [drastically from over 100,000 barrels per
day](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/01/17/world/americas/cuba-venezuela-oil-
power-blackouts.html) (bpd) to around 10,000 bpd in 2025. Since 2023,
[Mexico](https://www.ft.com/content/f04088c3-66af-4d7c-b5fd-df0e423bd837) has
also sent Cuba around 10,000 bpd per year, with Russia providing around 5,000
bpd in 2025. Amid the oil blockade, Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum has
instead shipped [humanitarian aid
](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/2/12/mexican-ships-arrive-in-cuba-with-
humanitarian-cargo-amid-us-oil-blockade)to the island while
[Moscow](https://thehill.com/policy/international/5735904-russia-cuba-fuel-
crisis-trump-tariffs/) has ignored US tariff threats.

In the past, Havana's tried-and-true method for dealing with internal unrest
was simply to [allow residents to emigrate to other
countries](https://www.american.edu/centers/latin-american-latino-
studies/upload/cuban-migration-and-its-social-crisis-an-overview.pdf); as many
as [3 million](https://english.elpais.com/international/2024-07-23/from-a-
population-of-11-million-to-little-more-than-85-million-the-real-toll-of-
cubas-migratory-crisis.html) Cubans are thought to have left the island since
the end of the COVID pandemic. In 2021, the Nicaraguan regime opted to remove
visa restrictions on its Bolivarian ally in Havana. This month, however,
Managua announced that it would [restore
](https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/nicaragua-scraps-visa-free-entry-
cubans-2026-02-08/)visa restrictions in an apparent effort to curry favor with
Washington.

In the view of the administration - and Miami neocons - deepening Cuba's
crisis while increasing the cost of emigration should finally provoke regime
change via popular uprising. In an Orwellian message to her constituents on
social media, GOP Congresswoman Maria Elvira Salazar, who represents Miami,
[reminded](https://x.com/MaElviraSalazar/status/2016898738216685672?s=20)
Cuban-Americans of their complicity in perpetuating the regime by sending aid
and remittances to family members on the island. She concluded by
[urging](https://x.com/MaElviraSalazar/status/2016898738216685672?s=20)
followers to look past a "suffering in the short term [and instead] free Cuba
once and for all."

Despicable as such statements and US policy towards Cuba may be, the reality
is that each serves a cynical strategic and electoral calculus. Following
Maduro's kidnapping in Venezuela, Rubio, Salazar, and a cabal of allied
[influencers](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rEn4sL7hvrg&t=3111s) and
activists in Miami have attempted to spin an otherwise bizarre symbiosis
between the Trump administration and the Bolivarian regime. Last week, Energy
Secretary Chris Wright [joined](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/2/12/us-
energy-secretary-chris-wright-touts-oil-production-on-venezuela-visit) interim
President Delcy Rodriguez for a visit to the oil production facilities for a
joint venture with Chevron in Venezuela, with no timeline for free and fair
elections in sight. In the eyes of MAGA and Bolivarian propagandists, both
Rodriguez and Trump are outsmarting one another. Yet for many rank-and-file
neoconservatives in Miami, little has fundamentally changed in Venezuela.

Trump's support among Latinos is currently in
[freefall](https://azpbs.org/horizonte/2026/02/poll-shows-majority-hispanic-
voters-disapprove-president-trump/), including a shocking nearly 20-point drop
among [Latino Republicans](https://www.theguardian.com/us-
news/2025/oct/25/trump-hispanic-approval-rating?ref=compactmag.com); in
December, a Democrat even won the mayor's race in
[Miami](https://www.compactmag.com/article/how-the-gop-lost-miami/) after more
than two decades of conservative leadership. By throttling Cuba, the
administration no doubt believes that it can shore up support among Latino
neocons ahead of the midterms and, more importantly, ensure its oil interests
in Venezuela. In his [own
words](https://www.realclearpolitics.com/video/2026/01/16/trump_on_why_hes_working_with_maduro_regime_i_remember_a_place_called_iraq.html),
Trump - and reportedly the [CIA](https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/cia-
concludes-regime-loyalists-best-suited-lead-venezuela-after-maduro-
wsj-2026-01-05/) - have assessed that a sudden and perhaps _any_ regime change
in Caracas runs the risk of creating a regional quagmire akin to Libya after
2011. In truth, this concern is more than [warranted,
](https://www.compactmag.com/article/regime-change-in-venezuela-is-bad-for-
america/)but ultimately matters little to the average neoconservative voter,
donor, or dissident activist in South Florida.

Were it not for the Miami lobby, it's ironically plausible that the president
would be open to a similar Frankenstein arrangement with the Cuban regime.
Trump had expressed interest in [opening a
hotel](https://theconversation.com/before-trump-was-anti-cuba-he-wanted-to-
open-a-hotel-in-havana-94689) in Cuba as far back as the 1990s, with members
of the Trump organization traveling to the island in 1998 as well as between
2012 and 2015. The president has [claimed ](https://apnews.com/article/cuba-
trump-oil-venezuela-talks-mexico-b4237de7a66adc4524a2abade5e0df38)that his
administration is currently in talks with Havana, which has expressed openness
towards dialogue but has denied the existence of actual negotiations. Last
week, Drop Site [reported](https://www.dropsitenews.com/p/marco-rubio-is-
deliberately-blocking) that Rubio deliberately misled the president about the
seemingly fictitious talks. On the other hand, it's equally plausible that
MAGA primacists like Stephen Miller and Trump himself are more concerned about
Cuban ties to [Beijing ](https://www.minnpost.com/community-
voices/2025/07/the-trump-team-ratchets-up-its-punishment-of-cuba/)and
[Tehran](https://abcnews.com/International/trump-threatens-tariffs-countries-
selling-oil-cuba-declaring/story?id=129687112).

Speaking with Bloomberg's John Micklethwait at the Munich Security Conference
this weekend, Rubio
[urged](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-02-14/rubio-says-cuba-s-
only-path-forward-is-to-open-its-
economy?utm_medium=email&utm_source=author_alert&utm_term=260214&utm_campaign=author_15109767)
Havana to embrace political and economic reform but declined to offer an
endgame for its broader Cuba policy. The secretary, it seems, is committed to
strangling the land of his forefathers in the name of ushering in "freedom" on
the island.
